text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- The Croatian embassy in Belgrade was stoned following the victory of Yugoslav basketball players against the Croatian national team.

- Two potential nuclear waste dump sites, one in Moslavacka Gora and the other in Trgovska Gora in the Banovina region southeast of Zagreb, are still being considered in line with an agreement between Croatia and Slovenia to both name one such location by the year 2002.
- More than 35,000 displaced people have registered for voucher privatisation. Registration ends on October 3.
- The state office for refugees and displaced people has received some 15,000 requests for the return to Eastern Slavonia.
- Hospitals are not paying their bills and this may cause a lack of medical supplies.
- First quarter budget revenues total 8.9 million kuna or 22.58 percent of the annual plan.
VECERNJI LIST
- Ivan Babic, a Croat, is named the new commander of the transitional police (TPF) in Eastern Slavonia. He replaces the retired commander of Serb origin Petar Djukic.
- The Zagreb archbishop Franjo Kuharic is to retire. His replacement to be announced next week.
- The American College of Management and Technology is opening a two-year study course in Dubrovnik in the autumn. Some 150 students will have to pay a $2,500 annual fee.
- One road worker was killed and another four injured when a mine exploded in Petrinja while they were clearing the road of weeds.
- We're the second most important bank for large enterprises, says Ante Todoric, president of the board of Kreditna Banka Zagreb.
- Money market: Interest rates fall thanks to good supply as liquidity of the banking sector improves.
- British cement group RMC plans to invest 100 million German marks into Dalmacijacement, which it bought for 34 million last month.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA

- A military agreement signed between Zagreb and Jerusalem in June includes not only the the buying and selling of arms but also a wider spectrum of cooperation that may result in the creation of new projects.
- The Adriatic Sea can produce 100,000 tonnes of health food a year, says Tomislav Vodopija, senior adviser for the fishing industry.
- Hotel Solitudo on the furthest Croatian island of Lastovo hopes for a return of tourists after six dry years. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
